answer: The quill multiplier is published, charged in karst, and wharf lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 519 identities would post 729 proofs and burn roughly 68 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
